newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai opens national shipping exchange.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai opens national shipping exchange.

text.p: China's first national shipping exchange opened on Thursday in Shanghai with 133 member companies enrolled, two of them foreign firms, officials said. Communications Minister Huang Zhendong banged the gong at a ceremony to mark the opening of the market in a building in the northern port area of the city.
The exchange has an electronic board displaying ships for sale or lease, with details of when and where they were built, their tonnage and speed, and details of incoming and outgoing cargoes.
On the wall reads a slogan "Fair, Open, Just".
The first deal concluded was for a Chinese domestic shipping line to deliver 17,000 tonnes of coal from a northern port to Shanghai, the Xinmin Evening News said.
Exchange officials declined to give trading details.
An official of one Chinese shipping company said the exchange provided a useful forum to follow prices, instead of relying on telephone contacts with individual companies.
The two foreign members are Maersk Shipping Co and one Hong Kong shipping firm, a notice in Thursday's Liberation Daily said.
Officials said earlier that the exchange would consolidate and standardise ship-chartering and cargo-fixing in east China and provide a focus for the shipping trade nationwide.
Shanghai ships more than 100 million tonnes of cargo to more than 400 ports in 170 countries and regions each year, according to official figures.
The Shanghai port expects to handle 1.9 million 20-foot containers in 1996, up from 1.5 million in 1995, they said.
